body.estimand_functional: Candidate critical inference target: \(\widehat\tau=(-\widehat a_T-\nabla\widehat\phi_T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\). The asserted Gaussian limit remains conditional on approval of a uniform harmonic reduced-cost nondegeneracy condition, correction and proof of the coupled nested derivative, and discharge of the uniform critical-control open question.

sampling_model.design: Four mutually independent repeated-cross-section samples indexed by \(g\in\{C0,C1,T0,T1\}\).
sampling_model.units: Within cell \(g\), \(X_{g,1},\ldots,X_{g,n_g}\) are independent draws from \(P_g\), with \(n=\min_g n_g\) and \(n_g/n\to\rho_g\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment group is untreated at period zero and exposed at period one; the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the no-treatment treated-post map from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell density is bounded between \(c\) and \(C\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), both nested Brenier Jacobians are uniformly elliptic, and the selected population lift branches remain \(\beta\)-separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the order-s signed periodized KDE followed by clipping and mass normalization. The proposed covariance algorithm is two-fold cross-fitted and retains harmonic scores and generated-target cross products, but its consistency awaits a valid coupled scalar--harmonic derivative and uniform moving-pole score bounds. The ridge still guarantees finite-sample block invertibility.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) only when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).
Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere boundary problem.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual law and map under cyclic comonotonicity, while the estimation section gives consistency rather than a sampling law.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify the gradient-Green contamination influence and its pole singularity; the abstract reports numerical stable-type fluctuations but the paper does not prove a shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.
Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound.
Theorem 18 gives the \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth density plug-in map without a matching logarithmic lower bound.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient influence functions and root-\(n\) cross-fitted inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data.

body.tldr: The note proves intrinsic torus changes-in-changes identification, the bandwidth arithmetic, and the fixed-center Green-aligned local lower bound. A new audit shows that the selected-lift derivative must couple each scalar Monge--Ampere equation to a two-dimensional transport-optimality equation. The frozen assumptions do not provide uniform nondegeneracy of those harmonic blocks, so the variable-coefficient covariance, Gaussian limit, adjoint covariance, ellipses, and uniform upper risk remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-path and uniform-law transport results do not provide either the finite-dimensional selected-harmonic derivative for a nested torus transport or the shrinking-bandwidth variable-coefficient Green control. The frozen scalar mass equations alone do not determine the harmonic increments.
project_justification.niche: The corrected architecture separates two finite-dimensional transport-optimality blocks from the scalar elliptic Green responses and retains all four cell noises and generated-target cross terms. Algebra fixes the candidate logarithmic covariance, but only after uniform harmonic invertibility and score stability are proved can it become an inference theorem.
project_justification.fill: The note currently supplies identification, the exact scalar propagation showing the omitted harmonic-divergence terms, a proposed uniform reduced-cost Hessian condition, the sharp mixed bandwidth calculation, the fixed-center lower-bound experiment, and conditional reductions for covariance, Gaussian approximation, adjoint estimation, coverage, and risk. It does not claim those conditional results as proved.

body.related_work: The Euclidean multivariate changes-in-changes paper motivates identification, while the present core separately proves its intrinsic torus identification lemma. The available fixed-path linearization does not determine or uniformly control the torus harmonic branch coordinates, and the published dimension-two Gaussian result covers only its stated uniform fixed-source case. Neither source closes the nested variable-coefficient harmonic or shrinking-bandwidth problem isolated here.
body.interpretation: At a prespecified treated-post location, the target remains the translation-aware no-treatment displacement. The four-cell expression with control weight \(\alpha\) and both treated-cell contributions is now an algebraically derived candidate covariance: it follows from local transformed-noise intensities, but its use for uncertainty quantification is conditional on the coupled harmonic and uniform Green estimates.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The first unresolved layer is finite dimensional: pointwise uniqueness and lift-branch separation do not imply a class-uniform lower bound for the reduced transport-cost Hessian in the harmonic coordinates. After that condition is resolved, the analysis must still prove the torus energy parametrix, nonlinear-versus-affine transformed-kernel remainder, moving-pole rate, opposite-fold score stability, fourth moments, and the two-endpoint mixed nested remainder. The broader upper bandwidth endpoint is not adopted while these steps remain open.
body.honest_scope: The established results cover intrinsic torus identification, bandwidth arithmetic, and a fixed-center logarithmic local lower bound under smooth positive four-cell sampling. No Gaussian approximation, feasible covariance theorem, simultaneous ellipse coverage, or class-uniform plug-in upper risk is presently claimed. Applying the proposal to a Card--Krueger bivariate reanalysis additionally requires a prespecified smooth periodic outcome construction, a defensible independent-cell approximation, approval or proof of harmonic branch nondegeneracy, and numerical errors below the eventual statistical scales.
